title: Festivals to consider for Malagasy filmmakers and producers
summary: A curated guide to Malagasy, African, Indian Ocean and international festivals relevant to films and projects connected to Madagascar.
editorialNote: This recovered starting selection is not a calendar of open submissions. Before submitting, confirm the festival is active and check eligible formats, premiere rules, fees, deadlines, screening rights and its official submission route.

entries.name: Rencontres du Film Court de Madagasikara
entries.description: Founded in 2006 in Antananarivo, the RFC combines screenings, professional exchange, training and the discovery of filmmakers. It developed into a pan-African short-film competition and is a central reference point for Malagasy short cinema.
entries.eligibility: Check the current edition's categories, territorial eligibility, film-completion window and submission dates.

entries.name: FESPACO
entries.description: The Pan-African Film and Television Festival of Ouagadougou is one of the continent's major cinema events. Malagasy works including L'Accident, Madame Esther and Zanaka, ainsi parlait Félix have received recognition there.
entries.eligibility: Consult the current regulations for African authorship and production requirements, categories, premiere conditions and deadlines.

entries.name: FIFAI — Festival International du Film d'Afrique et des Îles
entries.description: A festival in Réunion focused on films from Africa and island territories. Its Indian Ocean location makes it especially relevant to films from Madagascar; Ady Gasy received the Prix Fénèt Océan Indien there.
entries.eligibility: Confirm the current programme, accepted lengths and genres, submission method and dates with the organiser.

entries.name: African Film Festival Cologne — Jenseits von Europa
entries.description: Organised by FilmInitiativ in Cologne since 1992, this festival and its Africa Film Specials present contemporary and historical cinema from African countries to German audiences.
entries.eligibility: Ask the organiser about current programming priorities, screening formats, rights, fees and whether unsolicited submissions are accepted.

entries.name: Festival Lumières d'Afrique
entries.description: Created in Besançon in 1996, Lumières d'Afrique presents cinema from across the African continent. Ady Gasy received its documentary Grand Prix Eden in 2014.
entries.eligibility: Check current categories, submission route, production-date limits and conditions directly with the festival.

entries.name: FCAT — Festival de Cine Africano de Tarifa-Tánger
entries.region: Europe and Africa · Spain and Morocco
entries.description: Founded in 2004, FCAT is dedicated to African cinema and connects audiences and professionals across the Strait of Gibraltar. Malagasy Mankany received an audience award during the festival's Córdoba period.
entries.eligibility: Confirm the current edition's African-film definition, competitive sections, premiere policy and deadlines.

entries.name: Journées Cinématographiques de Carthage
entries.description: The Carthage Film Festival is a longstanding platform for African and Arab cinemas. Madame Esther was recognised at the JCC in 2015.
entries.eligibility: Review the current official regulations for eligible countries, sections, formats and deadlines.
